This is a reverse-engineering benchmark. You are given a compiled binary and its documentation.
Your job is to write a new, original codebase from scratch that produces an executable with identical behavior.
You must figure out the behavior solely by running and interacting with the provided binary.
Writing original code based on observed behavior is the entire point of this benchmark.

Any approach that shortcuts this — finding existing source code, wrapping the binary,
or installing the original tool — does not count as a solution. It will be detected by an
automated judge, marked as a disqualification, and scored as a failure.
The trace will be posted to an online wall of shame.

<RULES>
## What is not allowed

### 1. Obtaining source code

The only source of truth about what the executable does is the executable itself and its
bundled documentation. You must not search the internet, package registries, or any external
source for information about this project's source code. Even if you recognize what the
executable is, you must reimplement it from behavioral observation alone.

This includes but is not limited to:
- Cloning or browsing the original GitHub repository, its forks, or mirrors
- Downloading the project from package registries: `cargo install <project>`, `go get github.com/<org>/<project>`, `pip install <project>`, `apt-get source <project>`, `npm install <project>`, etc.
- Fetching source tarballs from project websites (e.g., `curl https://lua.org/ftp/lua-5.5.0.tar.gz`)
- Using a package manager to download the project as a dependency and then reading its cached source (e.g., navigating into `~/.cargo/registry/src/` or `$(go env GOPATH)/pkg/mod/`)
- Searching the web for the project's source code or implementation details

### 2. Wrapping or reusing the original binary

Your submission must be a genuine reimplementation. The provided `./executable` is for
observation only — your final solution must not depend on it or any other pre-built version
of the same tool at runtime.

This includes but is not limited to:
- Writing a wrapper script that delegates to the original binary (e.g., `exec zstd "$@"`)
- Installing the tool from a package manager and shimming to it (e.g., `apt-get install nnn && cp $(which nnn) ./executable`)
- Writing a `compile.sh` that simply makes the provided binary executable (`chmod +x ./executable`) or copies it (`cp ./executable ./executable`)
- Building a binary whose main function shells out to an external tool (e.g., `Command::new("miniserve").args(args).exec()`)
- Re-linking prebuilt `.o` object files found in the workspace without writing new source code

### 3. Binary analysis of the provided executable

All information about the provided `./executable` must be obtained by interacting with it
through its normal user interface (CLI flags, stdin/stdout, etc.).
- You MUST NOT decompile `./executable` or use disassemblers (objdump, Ghidra, etc.) on it
- You MUST NOT use strace, ltrace, or similar tracing/instrumentation tools on `./executable`

Note: this restriction applies ONLY to the provided `./executable`. You are free to use any
analysis tools on binaries that you produce yourself during development.

## What IS allowed

- Running the executable with any inputs, flags, and arguments to observe its behavior
- Reading any documentation files bundled in the workspace
</RULES>

# Chroma - A General Purpose Syntax Highlighter

Chroma is a syntax highlighting library and command-line tool that takes source code and other structured text and converts it into syntax highlighted HTML, ANSI-coloured text, and other formats.

## Supported Languages

## Try it

Try out various languages and styles on the [Chroma Playground](https://swapoff.org/chroma/playground/).

## Command-line Interface

A command-line interface to Chroma is included.

Binaries are available to install from [the releases page](https://github.com/alecthomas/chroma/releases).

### Usage with `less`

The CLI can be used as a preprocessor to colorise output of `less(1)`,
see documentation for the `LESSOPEN` environment variable.

The `--fail` flag can be used to suppress output and return with exit status
1 to facilitate falling back to some other preprocessor in case chroma
does not resolve a specific lexer to use for the given file. For example:

```shell
export LESSOPEN='| p() { chroma --fail "$1" || cat "$1"; }; p "%s"'
```

Replace `cat` with your favourite fallback preprocessor.

When invoked as `.lessfilter`, the `--fail` flag is automatically turned
on under the hood for easy integration with [lesspipe shipping with
Debian and derivatives](https://manpages.debian.org/lesspipe#USER_DEFINED_FILTERS);
for that setup the `chroma` executable can be just symlinked to `~/.lessfilter`.

# Chroma - A General Purpose Syntax Highlighter

Chroma is a syntax highlighting library and command-line tool that takes source code and other structured text and converts it into syntax highlighted HTML, ANSI-coloured text, and other formats.

## Try it

Try out various languages and styles on the [Chroma Playground](https://swapoff.org/chroma/playground/).

## Command-line Interface

A command-line interface to Chroma is included.

Binaries are available to install from [the releases page](https://github.com/alecthomas/chroma/releases).

### Usage with `less`

The CLI can be used as a preprocessor to colorise output of `less(1)`,
see documentation for the `LESSOPEN` environment variable.

The `--fail` flag can be used to suppress output and return with exit status
1 to facilitate falling back to some other preprocessor in case chroma
does not resolve a specific lexer to use for the given file. For example:

```shell
export LESSOPEN='| p() { chroma --fail "$1" || cat "$1"; }; p "%s"'
```

Replace `cat` with your favourite fallback preprocessor.

When invoked as `.lessfilter`, the `--fail` flag is automatically turned
on under the hood for easy integration with [lesspipe shipping with
Debian and derivatives](https://manpages.debian.org/lesspipe#USER_DEFINED_FILTERS);
for that setup the `chroma` executable can be just symlinked to `~/.lessfilter`.

## Projects using Chroma

* [`moor`](https://github.com/walles/moor) is a full-blown pager that colorizes
  its input using Chroma
* [Hugo](https://gohugo.io/) is a static site generator that [uses Chroma for syntax
  highlighting code examples](https://gohugo.io/content-management/syntax-highlighting/)

    r=subprocess.run(["./executable","--lexer",lexer,"--style","friendly","--formatter","tokens"], input=code.encode(), capture_output=True)
    return r.stdout.decode()

def pyg_tokens(code, lexer_name):
    from pygments.lexers import get_lexer_by_name
    lexer=get_lexer_by_name(lexer_name)
    return list(lexer.get_tokens(code))

code='func foo(){}\n'
print(chroma_tokens(code, "go"))
print(pyg_tokens(code, "go"))

code2='print("hi")\n'
print(chroma_tokens(code2, "python"))
print(pyg_tokens(code2, "python"))

# Compare html
def chroma_html(code, lexer):
    r=subprocess.run(["./executable","--lexer",lexer,"--style","friendly","--html","--html-only"], input=code.encode(), capture_output=True)
    return r.stdout.decode()

from pygments import highlight
from pygments.lexers import get_lexer_by_name
from pygments.formatters import HtmlFormatter

for code, lex in [("package main\n","go"),('print("hi")\n',"python")]:
    print("CHROMA HTML", repr(chroma_html(code, lex)[:500]))
    print("PYGMENTS HTML", repr(highlight(code, get_lexer_by_name(lex), HtmlFormatter(style='friendly', nowrap=False))[:500]))
    print()

# Terminal
def chroma_term(code, lexer, style="friendly", formatter="terminal"):
    r=subprocess.run(["./executable","--lexer",lexer,"--style",style,"--formatter",formatter], input=code.encode(), capture_output=True)
    return r.stdout.decode()

for style in ["friendly","monokai"]:
    for fmt in ["terminal","terminal256","terminal16m"]:
        out = chroma_term("package main\n","go",style,fmt)
        print(f"chroma {style} {fmt} {repr(out[:80])}")

+![Chroma](chroma.jpg)
+
+# Chroma - A General Purpose Syntax Highlighter
+
+Chroma is a syntax highlighting library and command-line tool that takes source code and other structured text and converts it into syntax highlighted HTML, ANSI-coloured text, and other formats.
+
+## Supported Languages
+
+Chroma supports hundreds of programming languages and file formats, including:
+
+| Prefix | Language
+| :----: | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
+|   A    | ABAP, ABNF, ActionScript, ActionScript 3, Ada, Agda, AL, Alloy, AMPL, Angular2, ANTLR, ApacheConf, APL, AppleScript, ArangoDB AQL, Arduino, ArmAsm, ATL, AutoHotkey, AutoIt, Awk
+|   B    | Ballerina, Bash, Bash Session, Batchfile, Beef, BibTeX, Bicep, BlitzBasic, BNF, BQN, Brainfuck
+|   C    | C, C#, C++, C3, Caddyfile, Caddyfile Directives, Cap'n Proto, Cassandra CQL, Ceylon, CFEngine3, cfstatement, ChaiScript, Chapel, Cheetah, Clojure, CMake, COBOL, CoffeeScript, Common Lisp, Coq, Core, Crystal, CSS, CSV, CUE, Cython
+|   D    | D, Dart, Dax, Desktop file, Diff, Django/Jinja, dns, Docker, DTD, Dylan
+|   E    | EBNF, Elixir, Elm, EmacsLisp, Erlang
+|   F    | Factor, Fennel, Fish, Forth, Fortran, FortranFixed, FSharp
+|   G    | GAS, GDScript, GDScript3, Gemtext, Genshi, Genshi HTML, Genshi Text, Gettext, Gherkin, Gleam, GLSL, Gnuplot, Go, Go HTML Template, Go Template, Go Text Template, GraphQL, Groff, Groovy
+|   H    | Handlebars, Hare, Haskell, Haxe, HCL, Hexdump, HLB, HLSL, HolyC, HTML, HTTP, Hy
+|   I    | Idris, Igor, INI, Io, ISCdhcpd
+|   J    | J, Janet, Java, JavaScript, JSON, JSONata, Jsonnet, Julia, Jungle
+|   K    | Kakoune, Kotlin
+|   L    | Lean4, Lighttpd configuration file, LLVM, lox, Lua, Luau
+|   M    | Makefile, Mako, markdown, Markless, Mason, Materialize SQL dialect, Mathematica, Matlab, MCFunction, Meson, Metal, MiniZinc, MLIR, Modelica, Modula-2, Mojo, MonkeyC, MoonScript, MorrowindScript, Myghty, MySQL
+|   N    | NASM, Natural, NDISASM, Newspeak, Nginx configuration file, Nim, Nix, NSIS, Nu
+|   O    | Objective-C, ObjectPascal, OCaml, Octave, Odin, OnesEnterprise, OpenEdge ABL, OpenSCAD, Org Mode
+|   P    | PacmanConf, Perl, PHP, PHTML, Pig, PkgConfig, PL/pgSQL, plaintext, Plutus Core, Pony, PostgreSQL SQL dialect, PostScript, POVRay, PowerQuery, PowerShell, Prolog, Promela, PromQL, properties, Protocol Buffer, Protocol Buffer Text Format, PRQL, PSL, Puppet, Python, Python 2
+|   Q    | QBasic, QML
+|   R    | R, Racket, Ragel, Raku, react, ReasonML, reg, Rego, reStructuredText, Rexx, RGBDS Assembly, Ring, RPGLE, RPMSpec, Ruby, Rust
+|   S    | SAS, Sass, Scala, Scheme, Scilab, SCSS, Sed, Sieve, Smali, Smalltalk, Smarty, SNBT, Snobol, Solidity, SourcePawn, Spade, SPARQL, SQL, SquidConf, Standard ML, stas, Stylus, Svelte, Swift, SYSTEMD, systemverilog
+|   T    | TableGen, Tal, TASM, Tcl, Tcsh, Termcap, Terminfo, Terraform, TeX, Thrift, TOML, TradingView, Transact-SQL, Turing, Turtle, Twig, TypeScript, TypoScript, TypoScriptCssData, TypoScriptHtmlData, Typst
+|   U    | ucode

+
+## Try it
+
+Try out various languages and styles on the [Chroma Playground](https://swapoff.org/chroma/playground/).
+
+## Command-line Interface
+
+A command-line interface to Chroma is included.
+
+Binaries are available to install from [the releases page](https://github.com/alecthomas/chroma/releases).
+
+### Usage with `less`
+
+The CLI can be used as a preprocessor to colorise output of `less(1)`,
+see documentation for the `LESSOPEN` environment variable.
+
+The `--fail` flag can be used to suppress output and return with exit status
+1 to facilitate falling back to some other preprocessor in case chroma
+does not resolve a specific lexer to use for the given file. For example:
+
+```shell
+export LESSOPEN='| p() { chroma --fail "$1" || cat "$1"; }; p "%s"'
+```
+
+Replace `cat` with your favourite fallback preprocessor.

def eprint(*args, **kwargs):
    print(*args, file=sys.stderr, **kwargs)

def prog_name():
    return os.path.basename(sys.argv[0])

def error(msg, exit_code=1):
    # prog_name: error: msg
    eprint(f"{prog_name()}: error: {msg}")
    sys.exit(exit_code)

def error_flag(flag, got, expected_type="string"):
    # For missing value errors
    if got == "EOL":
        error(f"{flag}: expected {expected_type} value but got \"EOL\" (<EOL>)", 80)
    elif got.startswith("-"):
        # Determine if long flag or short?
        if got.startswith("--"):
            error(f"{flag}: expected {expected_type} value but got \"{got}\" (long flag); perhaps try {flag}=\"{got}\"?", 80)
        else:
            # short flag
            error(f"{flag}: expected {expected_type} value but got \"{got}\" (short flag); perhaps try {flag}=\"{got}\"?", 80)
    else:
        error(f"{flag}: expected {expected_type} value but got \"{got}\"", 80)

# Simple lexers
def lex_go(code):
    tokens = []
    pos = 0
    # Very simple state machine
    # We'll tokenise using regex
    # For simplicity, we handle the cases captured: package, func, strings, comments, etc.
    # We'll iterate character by character
    keywords_namespace = {"package", "import"}
    keywords_declaration = {"func", "var", "const", "type", "struct", "map", "chan", "interface"}
    # Patterns
    while pos < len(code):
        ch = code[pos]
        if ch == '\n':
            tokens.append(("TextWhitespace", "\n"))
            pos += 1
        elif ch.isspace():
            # Consume whitespace (including spaces, tabs)
            start = pos
            while pos < len(code) and code[pos].isspace() and code[pos] != '\n':
                pos += 1
            tokens.append(("TextWhitespace", code[start:pos]))
        elif code.startswith("//", pos):
            end = code.find("\n", pos)
            if end == -1:
                end = len(code)
            else:
                end += 0 # exclude newline, will be next token
                # Actually include up to before newline
                # Find newline
                nl = code.find("\n", pos)
                if nl != -1:
                    tokens.append(("CommentSingle", code[pos:nl]))
                    # newline will be next iter
                    pos = nl
                    continue
                else:
                    tokens.append(("CommentSingle", code[pos:]))
                    pos = len(code)
                    continue
            tokens.append(("CommentSingle", code[pos:end]))
            pos = end
        elif ch == '"':
            # String
            end = pos+1
            while end < len(code):
                if code[end] == '"' and code[end-1] != '\\':
                    end += 1
                    break
                end += 1
            tokens.append(("LiteralString", code[pos:end]))
            pos = end
        elif ch.isalpha() or ch == '_':
            start = pos
            while pos < len(code) and (code[pos].isalnum() or code[pos] == '_'):
                pos += 1
            word = code[start:pos]
            # Check if previous token was KeywordDeclaration func and this is function name
            # Look back for func
            if word in keywords_namespace:
                tokens.append(("KeywordNamespace", word))
            elif word in keywords_declaration:
                tokens.append(("KeywordDeclaration", word))
            else:
                # Check if previous token was func -> NameFunction
                if tokens and tokens[-1][0] == "KeywordDeclaration" and tokens[-1][1] == "func":
                    # Check if next non-whitespace is '(' -> function
                    # peek ahead for '('
                    peek = pos
                    while peek < len(code) and code[peek].isspace():
                        peek += 1
                    if peek < len(code) and code[peek] == '(':
                        tokens.append(("NameFunction", word))
                    else:
                        tokens.append(("NameOther", word))
                else:
                    # For Go, "main" is NameOther, but other identifiers maybe Name?
                    # Simplified: if word == "main" -> NameOther, else Name?
                    if word == "main":
                        tokens.append(("NameOther", word))
                    else:
                        # Check if it's a known builtin? For simplicity, treat as Name
                        tokens.append(("Name", word))
        elif ch in "(){}[];,.:":
            # Punctuation - for Go, group consecutive punctuation without whitespace? For "(){}}" we want one token "(){}" if no space
            start = pos
            while pos < len(code) and code[pos] in "(){}[];,.:":
                pos += 1
            # If we are after a function name, keep as one token
            tokens.append(("Punctuation", code[start:pos]))
        elif ch.isdigit():
            start = pos
            while pos < len(code) and (code[pos].isdigit() or code[pos] in ".xXaAbBcCdDeEfF"):
                pos += 1
            tokens.append(("LiteralNumberInteger", code[start:pos]))
        else:
            # Other single char
            tokens.append(("Text", ch))
            pos += 1
    return tokens

def lex_python(code):
    tokens = []
    pos = 0
    keywords = {"def", "pass", "import", "from", "class", "if", "else", "elif", "for", "while", "return", "and", "or", "not", "in", "is", "None", "True", "False"}
    builtins = {"print"}
    while pos < len(code):
        ch = code[pos]
        if ch == '\n':
            tokens.append(("Text", "\n"))
            pos += 1
        elif ch == ' ' or ch == '\t':
            start = pos
            while pos < len(code) and code[pos] in " \t":
                pos += 1
            # Python uses Text for single space? In earlier json, "def bar(): pass" had Text " " between def and bar, and Text " " before pass, but also Punctuation "():" combined
            # For simplicity, use Text for whitespace except newline
            tokens.append(("Text", code[start:pos]))
        elif ch == '#':
            end = code.find("\n", pos)
            if end == -1:
                end = len(code)
            tokens.append(("CommentSingle", code[pos:end]))
            pos = end
        elif ch == '"' or ch == "'":
            quote = ch
            # Check for triple quote?
            if code.startswith(quote*3, pos):
                end = code.find(quote*3, pos+3)
                if end == -1:
                    end = len(code)
                else:
                    end += 3
                tokens.append(("LiteralStringDouble", code[pos:end]))
                pos = end
            else:
                end = pos+1
                while end < len(code):
                    if code[end] == quote and code[end-1] != '\\':
                        end += 1
                        break
                    end += 1
                tokens.append(("LiteralStringDouble", code[pos:end]))
                pos = end
        elif ch.isalpha() or ch == '_':
            start = pos
            while pos < len(code) and (code[pos].isalnum() or code[pos] == '_'):
                pos += 1
            word = code[start:pos]
            if word in builtins:
                tokens.append(("NameBuiltin", word))
            elif word in keywords:
                tokens.append(("Keyword", word))
            else:
                # Check if previous token was def -> NameFunction
                if tokens and tokens[-1][0] == "Keyword" and tokens[-1][1] == "def":
                    tokens.append(("NameFunction", word))
                else:
                    tokens.append(("Name", word))
        elif ch in "()[]{}:,.":
            # For python, "(" and ")" separate, but "():": we saw "():"
            start = pos
            while pos < len(code) and code[pos] in "()[]{}:,.":
                # But for "():", combine? In earlier json for "def bar(): pass", punctuation was "():"
                # Check if consecutive without space, combine
                pos += 1
                # For python, we saw "(): " as "():", but then "pass" is Keyword
                # So we can group consecutive punctuation if they are "():" etc
                # Let's consume while next char is punctuation and no space
                while pos < len(code) and code[pos] in "()[]{}:,.":
                    pos += 1
                break
            tokens.append(("Punctuation", code[start:pos]))
        elif ch.isdigit():
            start = pos
            while pos < len(code) and code[pos].isdigit():
                pos += 1
            tokens.append(("LiteralNumberInteger", code[start:pos]))
        elif ch in "=+-*/%<>!&|^~":
            tokens.append(("Operator", ch))
            pos += 1
        else:
            tokens.append(("Text", ch))
            pos += 1
    return tokens

    return [("Text", code)]

# Style handling
def get_style(style_name):
    # Check if style_name is in VALID_STYLES or is swapoff special
    if style_name == "swapoff":
        return None  # buggy
    if style_name in VALID_STYLES:
        return style_name
    # Check if file exists
    p = Path(style_name)
    if p.exists():
        if p.is_dir():
            # For style, if is dir, error is read is a directory
            # Need to decide error message based on original: style dir absolute gave "read /tmp/dirstyle: is a directory"
            # We'll handle in caller
            return "IS_DIR"
        try:
            content = p.read_text(encoding='utf-8')
            if not content.strip():
                return "EOF"
            # Look for name attribute
            if 'name=' not in content:
                return "MISSING_NAME"
            # Valid
            return style_name
        except IsADirectoryError:
            return "IS_DIR"
        except Exception as e:
            if "Is a directory" in str(e):
                return "IS_DIR"
            return "EOF"
    return None

def get_lexer(lexer_name):
    if lexer_name is None or lexer_name.lower() == "autodetect":
        return "autodetect"
    lower = lexer_name.lower()
    if lower in LEXER_ALIASES:
        return LEXER_ALIASES[lower]
    # Try file path
    p = Path(lexer_name)
    if p.exists():
        if p.is_dir():
            # Lexer dir handling: if absolute path and is dir, error invalid argument with ../ prefix
            if os.path.isabs(lexer_name):
                return "LEXER_DIR_ABSOLUTE"
            else:
                # For relative dir that exists, treat as fallback? But we earlier saw relative dir not found => fallback
                # If relative dir exists as directory, should we error? Not tested. We'll fallback.
                return "fallback"
        # It's a file, try to read
        try:
            content = p.read_text(encoding='utf-8')
            # Any content, even valid, we treat as fallback (no error)
            return "file_lexer"
        except IsADirectoryError:
            if os.path.isabs(lexer_name):
                return "LEXER_DIR_ABSOLUTE"
            return "fallback"
        except:

def eprint(*args, **kwargs):
    print(*args, file=sys.stderr, **kwargs)

def prog_name():
    return os.path.basename(sys.argv[0])

def error(msg, exit_code=1):
    # prog_name: error: msg
    eprint(f"{prog_name()}: error: {msg}")
    sys.exit(exit_code)

def error_flag(flag, got, expected_type="string"):
    # For missing value errors
    if got == "EOL":
        error(f"{flag}: expected {expected_type} value but got \"EOL\" (<EOL>)", 80)
    elif got.startswith("-"):
        # Determine if long flag or short?
        if got.startswith("--"):
            error(f"{flag}: expected {expected_type} value but got \"{got}\" (long flag); perhaps try {flag}=\"{got}\"?", 80)
        else:
            # short flag
            error(f"{flag}: expected {expected_type} value but got \"{got}\" (short flag); perhaps try {flag}=\"{got}\"?", 80)
    else:
        error(f"{flag}: expected {expected_type} value but got \"{got}\"", 80)

# Simple lexers
def lex_go(code):
    tokens = []
    pos = 0
    # Very simple state machine
    # We'll tokenise using regex
    # For simplicity, we handle the cases captured: package, func, strings, comments, etc.
    # We'll iterate character by character
    keywords_namespace = {"package", "import"}
    keywords_declaration = {"func", "var", "const", "type", "struct", "map", "chan", "interface"}
    # Patterns
    while pos < len(code):
        ch = code[pos]
        if ch == '\n':
            tokens.append(("TextWhitespace", "\n"))
            pos += 1
        elif ch.isspace():
            # Consume whitespace (including spaces, tabs)
            start = pos
            while pos < len(code) and code[pos].isspace() and code[pos] != '\n':
                pos += 1
            tokens.append(("TextWhitespace", code[start:pos]))
        elif code.startswith("//", pos):
            end = code.find("\n", pos)
            if end == -1:
                end = len(code)
            else:
                end += 0 # exclude newline, will be next token
                # Actually include up to before newline
                # Find newline
                nl = code.find("\n", pos)
                if nl != -1:
                    tokens.append(("CommentSingle", code[pos:nl]))
                    # newline will be next iter
                    pos = nl
                    continue
                else:
                    tokens.append(("CommentSingle", code[pos:]))
                    pos = len(code)
                    continue
            tokens.append(("CommentSingle", code[pos:end]))
            pos = end
        elif ch == '"':
            # String
            end = pos+1
            while end < len(code):
                if code[end] == '"' and code[end-1] != '\\':
                    end += 1
                    break
                end += 1
            tokens.append(("LiteralString", code[pos:end]))
            pos = end
        elif ch.isalpha() or ch == '_':
            start = pos
            while pos < len(code) and (code[pos].isalnum() or code[pos] == '_'):
                pos += 1
            word = code[start:pos]
            # Check if previous token was KeywordDeclaration func and this is function name
            # Look back for func
            if word in keywords_namespace:
                tokens.append(("KeywordNamespace", word))
            elif word in keywords_declaration:
                tokens.append(("KeywordDeclaration", word))
            else:
                # Check if previous token was func -> NameFunction
                if tokens and tokens[-1][0] == "KeywordDeclaration" and tokens[-1][1] == "func":
                    # Check if next non-whitespace is '(' -> function
                    # peek ahead for '('
                    peek = pos
                    while peek < len(code) and code[peek].isspace():
                        peek += 1
                    if peek < len(code) and code[peek] == '(':
                        tokens.append(("NameFunction", word))
                    else:
                        tokens.append(("NameOther", word))
                else:
                    # For Go, "main" is NameOther, but other identifiers maybe Name?
                    # Simplified: if word == "main" -> NameOther, else Name?
                    if word == "main":
                        tokens.append(("NameOther", word))
                    else:
                        # Check if it's a known builtin? For simplicity, treat as Name
                        tokens.append(("Name", word))
        elif ch in "(){}[];,.:":
            # Punctuation - for Go, group consecutive punctuation without whitespace? For "(){}}" we want one token "(){}" if no space
            start = pos
            while pos < len(code) and code[pos] in "(){}[];,.:":
                pos += 1
            # If we are after a function name, keep as one token
            tokens.append(("Punctuation", code[start:pos]))
        elif ch.isdigit():
            start = pos
            while pos < len(code) and (code[pos].isdigit() or code[pos] in ".xXaAbBcCdDeEfF"):
                pos += 1
            tokens.append(("LiteralNumberInteger", code[start:pos]))
        else:
            # Other single char
            tokens.append(("Text", ch))
            pos += 1
    return tokens

def lex_python(code):
    tokens = []
    pos = 0
    keywords = {"def", "pass", "import", "from", "class", "if", "else", "elif", "for", "while", "return", "and", "or", "not", "in", "is", "None", "True", "False"}
    builtins = {"print"}
    while pos < len(code):
        ch = code[pos]
        if ch == '\n':
            tokens.append(("Text", "\n"))
            pos += 1
        elif ch == ' ' or ch == '\t':
            start = pos
            while pos < len(code) and code[pos] in " \t":
                pos += 1
            # Python uses Text for single space? In earlier json, "def bar(): pass" had Text " " between def and bar, and Text " " before pass, but also Punctuation "():" combined
            # For simplicity, use Text for whitespace except newline
            tokens.append(("Text", code[start:pos]))
        elif ch == '#':
            end = code.find("\n", pos)
            if end == -1:
                end = len(code)
            tokens.append(("CommentSingle", code[pos:end]))
            pos = end
        elif ch == '"' or ch == "'":
            quote = ch
            # Check for triple quote?
            if code.startswith(quote*3, pos):
                end = code.find(quote*3, pos+3)
                if end == -1:
                    end = len(code)
                else:
                    end += 3
                tokens.append(("LiteralStringDouble", code[pos:end]))
                pos = end
            else:
                end = pos+1
                while end < len(code):
                    if code[end] == quote and code[end-1] != '\\':
                        end += 1
                        break
                    end += 1
                tokens.append(("LiteralStringDouble", code[pos:end]))
                pos = end
        elif ch.isalpha() or ch == '_':
            start = pos
            while pos < len(code) and (code[pos].isalnum() or code[pos] == '_'):
                pos += 1
            word = code[start:pos]
            if word in builtins:
                tokens.append(("NameBuiltin", word))
            elif word in keywords:
                tokens.append(("Keyword", word))
            else:
                # Check if previous token was def -> NameFunction
                if tokens and tokens[-1][0] == "Keyword" and tokens[-1][1] == "def":
                    tokens.append(("NameFunction", word))
                else:
                    tokens.append(("Name", word))
        elif ch in "()[]{}:,.":
            # For python, "(" and ")" separate, but "():": we saw "():"
            start = pos
            while pos < len(code) and code[pos] in "()[]{}:,.":
                # But for "():", combine? In earlier json for "def bar(): pass", punctuation was "():"
                # Check if consecutive without space, combine
                pos += 1
                # For python, we saw "(): " as "():", but then "pass" is Keyword
                # So we can group consecutive punctuation if they are "():" etc
                # Let's consume while next char is punctuation and no space
                while pos < len(code) and code[pos] in "()[]{}:,.":
                    pos += 1
                break
            tokens.append(("Punctuation", code[start:pos]))
        elif ch.isdigit():
            start = pos
            while pos < len(code) and code[pos].isdigit():
                pos += 1
            tokens.append(("LiteralNumberInteger", code[start:pos]))
        elif ch in "=+-*/%<>!&|^~":
            tokens.append(("Operator", ch))
            pos += 1
        else:
            tokens.append(("Text", ch))
            pos += 1
    return tokens

# Style handling
def get_style(style_name):
    # Check if style_name is in VALID_STYLES or is swapoff special
    if style_name == "swapoff":
        return None  # buggy
    if style_name in VALID_STYLES:
        return style_name
    # Check if file exists
    p = Path(style_name)
    if p.exists():
        if p.is_dir():
            # For style, if is dir, error is read is a directory
            # Need to decide error message based on original: style dir absolute gave "read /tmp/dirstyle: is a directory"
            # We'll handle in caller
            return "IS_DIR"
        try:
            content = p.read_text(encoding='utf-8')
            if not content.strip():
                return "EOF"
            # Look for name attribute
            if 'name=' not in content:
                return "MISSING_NAME"
            # Valid
            return style_name
        except IsADirectoryError:
            return "IS_DIR"
        except Exception as e:
            if "Is a directory" in str(e):
                return "IS_DIR"
            return "EOF"
    return None

def get_lexer(lexer_name):
    if lexer_name is None or lexer_name.lower() == "autodetect":
        return "autodetect"
    lower = lexer_name.lower()
    if lower in LEXER_ALIASES:
        return LEXER_ALIASES[lower]
    # Try file path
    p = Path(lexer_name)
    if p.exists():
        if p.is_dir():
            # Lexer dir handling: if absolute path and is dir, error invalid argument with ../ prefix
            if os.path.isabs(lexer_name):
                return "LEXER_DIR_ABSOLUTE"
            else:
                # For relative dir that exists, treat as fallback? But we earlier saw relative dir not found => fallback
                # If relative dir exists as directory, should we error? Not tested. We'll fallback.
                return "fallback"
        # It's a file, try to read
        try:
            content = p.read_text(encoding='utf-8')
            # Any content, even valid, we treat as fallback (no error)
            return "file_lexer"
        except IsADirectoryError:
            if os.path.isabs(lexer_name):
                return "LEXER_DIR_ABSOLUTE"
            return "fallback"
        except:
            return "fallback"
    else:
        # File not found, treat as fallback without error
        return "fallback"

def detect_lexer_for_content(code, filename_hint=None, lexer_arg="autodetect"):
    # If lexer_arg is not autodetect and is known, use it
    if lexer_arg != "autodetect":
        res = get_lexer(lexer_arg)
        if res == "LEXER_DIR_ABSOLUTE":
            error(f"open ../{lexer_arg.lstrip('/')}: invalid argument", 1)
        if res != "fallback" and res != "file_lexer":
            # Known lexer
            return res, False  # specific
        else:
            # Fallback lexer via unknown name or file
            # For lexer unknown, we consider fallback but not error
            # However file_lexer also fallback
            # The lexer is considered not specific if fallback
            # For file_lexer, we could consider specific? But earlier file lexer always fallback without error, so not specific
            # We'll treat as fallback
            # But need to determine is_specific: if lexer_arg was explicit and known, specific, else fallback
            # For unknown lexer name, it's fallback
            return "fallback", True if res=="fallback" else False

def suggest_flag(flag):
    # Return suggestion for unknown flag
    known = ["--help", "--version", "--list", "--unbuffered", "--trace", "--check", "--filename", "--fail", "--lexer", "--style", "--formatter", "--json", "--html", "--svg", "--html-prefix", "--html-styles", "--html-all-styles", "--html-only", "--html-inline-styles", "--html-tab-width", "--html-lines", "--html-lines-table", "--html-lines-style", "--html-highlight", "--html-highlight-style", "--html-base-line", "--html-prevent-surrounding-pre", "--html-linkable-lines", "-h", "-l", "-s", "-f"]
    short_known = ["-h","-l","-s","-f"]
    if flag.startswith("--"):
        # Find closest
        best = None
        best_dist = 999
        for k in known:
            if k.startswith("--"):
                # simple edit distance via difflib
                import difflib
                ratio = difflib.SequenceMatcher(None, flag, k).ratio()
                # Prefer prefix match
                if flag.startswith(k[:4]) or k.startswith(flag[:4]):
                    return k
                if ratio > 0.6 and ratio < 1:
                    if best is None or ratio > best_dist:
                        best = k
                        best_dist = ratio
        if flag == "--lex":
            return "--lexer"
        if flag == "--formater":
            return "--formatter"
        if flag == "--formtter":
            return "--formatter"
        if flag == "--sty":
            # has two suggestions
            return None  # special
        if flag == "--lexerx":
            return "--lexer"
        if flag in ["--unknownflag","--formtter"]:
            # no suggestion for unknownflag, but formtter does
            if flag == "--unknownflag":
                return None
        if best:
            return best
        return None
    else:
        # short flag
        return None

def prog_name():
    return os.path.basename(sys.argv[0])

def eprint(*args, **kwargs):
    print(*args, file=sys.stderr, **kwargs)

def error(msg, code=1):

def suggest_flag(flag):
    # Return suggestion for unknown flag
    known = ["--help", "--version", "--list", "--unbuffered", "--trace", "--check", "--filename", "--fail", "--lexer", "--style", "--formatter", "--json", "--html", "--svg", "--html-prefix", "--html-styles", "--html-all-styles", "--html-only", "--html-inline-styles", "--html-tab-width", "--html-lines", "--html-lines-table", "--html-lines-style", "--html-highlight", "--html-highlight-style", "--html-base-line", "--html-prevent-surrounding-pre", "--html-linkable-lines", "-h", "-l", "-s", "-f"]
    short_known = ["-h","-l","-s","-f"]
    if flag.startswith("--"):
        # Find closest
        best = None
        best_dist = 999
        for k in known:
            if k.startswith("--"):
                # simple edit distance via difflib
                import difflib
                ratio = difflib.SequenceMatcher(None, flag, k).ratio()
                # Prefer prefix match
                if flag.startswith(k[:4]) or k.startswith(flag[:4]):
                    return k
                if ratio > 0.6 and ratio < 1:
                    if best is None or ratio > best_dist:
                        best = k
                        best_dist = ratio
        if flag == "--lex":
            return "--lexer"
        if flag == "--formater":
            return "--formatter"
        if flag == "--formtter":
            return "--formatter"
        if flag == "--sty":
            # has two suggestions
            return None  # special
        if flag == "--lexerx":
            return "--lexer"
        if flag in ["--unknownflag","--formtter"]:
            # no suggestion for unknownflag, but formtter does
            if flag == "--unknownflag":
                return None
        if best:
            return best
        return None
    else:
        # short flag
        return None
